record.name: Caretaker Supplement
record.administeredBy: Wisconsin Department of Health Services / Department of Children and Families (paid with the state SSI payment; applications through county and Tribal agencies)
record._categoriesNote: A cash benefit for SSI-recipient parents raising minor children -- 'childcare-education' and 'food-basic-needs' both partly fit; neither squarely.
record.summary: A monthly cash benefit for parents who receive Wisconsin SSI and are living with and caring for their own minor children.
record.benefit: $275 per month for the first eligible child and $165 per month for each additional eligible child, paid as part of the parent's monthly state SSI payment.

steps: Apply online through ACCESS, by phone, mail (form F-22571), or in person at your county or Tribal agency.
Confirm you receive a Wisconsin SSI payment and are living with your minor children.
Cooperate with the child support agency regarding any absent parent.

of._sourceText: Your household must meet some nonfinancial criteria, such as Wisconsin residency.
You must be getting a Wisconsin SSI payment. (Handbook: if the entire SSI payment is being recouped, the parent does not qualify.)
Are living with and caring for your minor children
Your children must meet income and asset requirements.
You cannot get CTS benefits for any of your children who are also receiving SSI.

of.note: If the child has two parents in the household, BOTH parents must be receiving Wisconsin SSI. Not decidable without knowing household composition and each parent's SSI status.

factsNeeded.sourceText: getting a Wisconsin SSI payment -- currentBenefits has 'ssi', but this is specifically the WISCONSIN state SSI supplement, and 'not being fully recouped'
living with and caring for your minor children -- hasChildUnder5 / hasSchoolAgeChild are close but do not assert the respondent is the parent, nor 'minor' (under 18)
Your children must meet income and asset requirements -- a child-level financial test, like Katie Beckett's 'income in their name'
any of your children who are also receiving SSI

cost.notes: 2 fetches + 1 search. The citizen page carries a clean eligibility list; the handbook fetch was to confirm the child-financial-test and two-parent rule exist, not to transcribe thresholds.

surprises: Third candidate (with Katie Beckett and, loosely, FPOS) whose income test is on the CHILD or the APPLICANT specifically, not 'the household'. incomeAtOrBelow() and annualHouseholdIncome assume a single household aggregate; a recurring pattern in the corpus is rules that scope income to a person within the household.
